notes.title: 🌸 Haunted Arcade - Blooming Update! 🌸
notes.content:
Heyo! I wanted to give a quick update to confirm that I'm still working on stuff.
I'm currently knees-deep into a fundamental update for Hooked on Art, and it is taking a lot of energy, but I really needed to put out something, anything at all, for my own sanity and to eliminate any time pressures, so here's an Update with all the non-Hooked-on-Art changes that I've made so far! :)
They might not be that much compared to previous updates, but I promise that new content will come!

Changes:

 Blooming Furniture: In the Storage Room, there's something new waiting - a flower! If you interact with it, you can place it freely around the Hall to decorate.
 Blooming Hat: The free Hat of the season is the Flower Hat! Equip it onto the Ghost by heading to the Ticket Shop and interacting with the shopkeeper. :)
 General: I removed DRM Protection. By default, the Steam API has a DRM system quitting the game when false launches are detected. I've removed this for several reasons, some of which include ease of use and to prevent crashes through false-positives. So feel free to send this game to your friend!
 UI: The game can now automatically detect the input device you have last used! If you press any key or mouse button, the input device is seen as keyboard, and if you press any controller button, the input device is seen as gamepad! All primary UI gets changed - eg. the floating the A button transforms into the [E] Key!
 Boot-Up: I've added the Splash Screens for our Development Studio as well as my Publishing Initiative. :) These are the same Splash Screens that are on Hidden Arcade already!
 Code: I've optimized some performance heavy code in some scripts that were written very early on, the game should run a bit better now :)


So as I've said, I am currently working on a major Hooked on Art update, aiming to not only make it work better, but also to make it feel more like the finale to the game. I've self-imposed a deadline of March 31st for this, but I am very doubtful that I will be able to meet this.
So instead, I've been thinking of a few other things I can hit first.
As such, I have put together this patch right now, and something else that is going to release in the next few days (maybe tomorrow) is a "Blossom Update" for Spring / Summer to replace the Christmas/Winter Update, that might be coming in the next few days as well! Stay tuned c:

Happy Christmas! For this theme, I have opened up the storage room of the shop, granting access to the Christmas Tree as well as two Presents! Additionally, I've added several Fan Elements that were requested by the community! :)

notes.title: A New Free Game in the Haunted Arcade Universe!
notes.content:
Heyo! My partner and I have been working on our newest project, and it's finally here! You can find out more about it in this video:

[previewyoutube=M-K9hIP3kO8;full][/previewyoutube]
You can find it here: Get Hidden Arcade Now For Free!

Q: What is this game about?
A: 💗 Find and free the hidden Ghosts spread throughout distinct Arcade Game Worlds, and create your own ones! 💗
Hidden Arcade is a Hidden Object point-and-click game in which the player has to find Ghosts inside of different Arcade Machines! ✨

Q: Why this game and not any other hidden object game?
A: The game's unique selling factor is that it innovates on the genre in many ways:
1) To add replayability, each level has a timer as well as a global leaderboard so that people can improve their times! You can of course turn it off if you would like a more relaxed experience. ✨
2) To add functionality, people can create their own levels using the Custom Creator! Pick your own background image, drag Ghosts around, scale them and exchange each Ghost's texture, insert custom sounds, give it a name and upload it to the Steam Workshop! ✨
3) To add community, everyone can download user-created levels and play them in the Custom Player! Clicking on any slot that says "Get more..." leads you straight to the Steam Workshop where you can subscribe to any levels you would like to play. Hitting refresh when you're back in the game will show all your new levels and allow you to enjoy them! ✨
4) To add color to the world, this game is available in color! This might not sound that big, but the vast majority of "100 xxx in xxx" games are black and white only. This game features beautiful artwork that took hours to complete, and you can choose whether to view it through a black-and-white lens, or to see all the colors it was drawn in! ✨ 

Q: Why should I get the game now?
A: For the Release Week, the Custom Creator is available to everyone! Just boot up the game and start making your own levels - don't worry, you'll be able to play user-created levels for free forever! But on Monday the 10th, the Custom Creator will be released as a DLC for 99 Cents instead. I would love to keep the game entirely free forever, but sadly, I need to insert some way to make back the 100 Dollars it cost to get the game on Steam, and I poured hundreds of unpaid hours into it. I hope that 99 cents for an optional level editor in a free game is an okay price to pay.

Q: I found an issue. What should I do?
A: Please tell me! Either in the Discussions form, or via email, you can tell me any feature you'd like, any bug you found, and I will try to address them as soon as possible!

Q: How could I possibly support such a fantastic free game?
A: Great that you're asking! If you can claim the game to add it to your library, let it run in the background and/or write a review for it, that would massively help me by boosting it in the almighty algorithm!

Q: Why did you make this game?
A: I've had a very sudden fixation on Hidden Object games of the type of "100 xxx in xxx" last year and knew that I wanted to make one that is made with genuine love and care due to the oversaturation of poorly optimized, quickly developed slop. My partner was instantly on board and provided her amazing drawing skills. This is the result of that. :D

Alrighty that's everything for now I guess, hope u enjoy and ya!
Don't worry, this doesn't mean I won't work on Haunted Arcade anymore. Still planning to overwork Hooked on Art :)
So see ya around and ya, goodbyeoo!

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - R1.22.4 Patch
notes.content:
Heyo! It's been a bit, happy new year! Been keeping busy. Here's how it's looking today: :)

Bugfixes:


 Arcade Hall: Fixed the Hub music no longer playing when exiting an Arcade Game. Exiting any Arcade Game will restart the Hub music every time now.
 Arcade Hall: Added a permanent save system for the relation to the Ghost. Previously, exiting to the Main Menu and then continuing reset your relation meter. It no longer does. I've thus also added a Reset when starting a New Game.
 Arcade Hall: Fixed the Interact Circle Indicator for the Shop disappearing / missing.
 Arcade Hall: Added a coroutine that clears all unused assets from cashe every 15 seconds while the player is not playing an Arcade Game, as well as immediately after exiting an Arcade Game. Since some people are still experiencing crashes, this is another attempt at combatting that. As is the next point!
 General: Removed significant amount of Warnings, as well as unused code. The project previously had 30 Warnings (not errors, 0 errors), now it has 6 Warnings. The remaining warnings come from the use of obsolete code in a Scriptable Render Feature, and from Wwise / Audio. If the crashes remain, it kind of has to be one of the two.


Other:


 Arcade Hall: Players can no longer jump while carrying (heavy) objects. This also fixes the bug of players being able to float when holding objects underneath them and jumping.

notes.title: 🎃 Haunted Arcade - Halloween Update! 🎃
notes.content:
Happy Halloween! For this month only, you can get the Halloween Texture Set by just walking up to the Spraycan at the counter, without having to earn 30 tickets first. In addition to that, it's expanded, with all-new textures for Arcade Machines!

Before we get into the update news, a quick disclaimer / roadmap:
It's been about two months since our initial Release, and one month since the last Update / Patch. Most of the team has gone on with their studies and is working on different games right now. Since this is not a lucrative business, we do not have the budget to hire someone to work on it nor the ability to spend all our time on it, and so continuously working on updates is not possible for me right now. Thus, I've decided to limit it to one (major) update a month, excluding patches. This month is the Halloween Update! Next month, I would like to do the Fan Update and incorporate anyone who has won or been promised a digital custom hat or some other in-game item. And after that, it's Christmas already. :)
Most post-launch changes to this game come directly from me. The exception to that is the Laser Bike Arcade Game, whose developer also found some time to bring you some changes. :)

Now, let's get into it!

Headlines:

 Halloween: For this month, and this month only, you can activate the Halloween Set by just walking up to the Spraycan directly (instead of having to earn 30 tickets first). But not only that! Because:
 Texture Sets: The Halloween and Aqua Set have a vast amount of new hand-drawn textures for Arcade Machines! These textures now also apply to dirty Arcade Machines. Feel free to check them out. :)
 Save System: Since this has been an issue commonly pointed out in recent reviews, I am trying to make the permanent Save System as smooth and accurate as possible! Specifically, first of, if the lights get turned off by the Ghost, they now stay off if you quit the game and then continue it. Second, all Arcade Games lock after beating them, but they would unlock again by quitting and continuing. Now, they stay locked. If you want further details to that, look into the Bugfixes Section!


Quality of Life:

 Corrected several typos in the Hub Area and grammatical issues in Laser Bike.


Bugfixes

 Save System as mentioned in Headlines Section. Further Details: The Story Progression works by beating any Arcade Game. Beating any one of them will continue the story. Now normally, they get locked after beating them, so that you have to play the others. But if you quit and hit Continue from the Main Menu, all Arcades would be unlocked again. Due to that, you could beat the same game multiple times and traverse the entire story through that. This issue has been addressed so that they stay locked.
 Major Performance Improvements in the Laser Bike Arcade Game due to a rework of its structure!
 Fixed issue with wrench not unlocking from Shop after first Arcade Game
 And many more fixes! :D


I think that is everything for now. Thanks for reading this, and I hope I can make any bugs and issues up to you through this update as well as future patches. - Lem ^^

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - R1.09 Patch
notes.content:
Bugfixes:


 Story Mode: I've rewritten a large part of a heavy script in the Hub Scene, responsible for Ghost interactions and progression. It is now about 350 lines shorter while still fulfilling the same function, and several frame-based or computationally very intensive Unity functions have been replaced with different ones, which should result in a more consistent frame rate / less drops on cutscenes, as well as slightly less CPU usage.
 Any Mode: I have tweaked a few lighting settings and removed unused Render Assets, resulting in a 20% frame increase on my PC.
 Story Mode: The 7th Arcade Game bugged out for several people when it unlocked after beating the previous 6 games, but no longer! The trigger for it now remains active and prompts the locked icon whenever the player tries interacting with it before beating the previous 6 games.
 Story Mode: Automatically saving the player's quest progress for when selecting the Continue option in the main menu now works up until the last Arcade Game. 
 And several more fixes!


Have a good one and hope you enjoy ^^

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - R1.08 Patch
notes.content:
Bugfixes:


 Story Mode: Reworked the Core Struture of the Arcade Game Implementation - saves about 23% or 504MB of RAM on average. Planning on continuing this technique in future patches to optimize memory usage in order to prevent crashes on lower-end or falsely allocated hardware.
 Arcade Mode: Back button properly leads back to the Main Menu.
 Arcade Mode: Escaping out of an Arcade Game properly leads back to the Quick Selection.
 Story Mode: UI Overlays fixed - speech bubbles can no longer overlay Arcade Games or the Shop.
 Story Mode: Laser Bike and Sheepy Runs! now feature less bent screen curvatures to prevent motion  sickness.
 Story Mode: The screens of the Arcade Machines now get re-activated after fixing the power. Also, whenever you are not playing the Arcade Game, they are properly displaying the Arcade Game's Start Menu now.
 Story Mode: On KBM, A and D could flip the pages in the Escape Menu. However, they are also necessary to get to the sliders on the Settings Tab. That is why they have been removed from flipping pages. You can still do so on KBM by either pressing 1 or 3 or F1 or F3 to go left or right, or pressing Tab to cycle through.
 Any Mode: Music properly gets reset when going back to the Main Menu.
 Credits: Removed Early Access paragraph.
 And several more fixes!


Sorry for ditching the "No more!" style I used to try and keep consistent with past patches, it just came to a point where it limits the clarity of the actual fix / content.

Have a good one and hope you enjoy ^^

notes.title: ✨ Haunted Arcade - RELEASE 1.0! ✨
notes.content:
It is time - three new Arcade Games, making for a total of 7!
As you are reading this, we are packing our things, getting going to Cologne and setting up our booth in Hall 10.2. And this also marks our arrival at a version we feel comfortable with calling a Release 1.0!

There are three new Arcade Games, an overworked Arcade Mode, an extended Story and more!

Headlines:

 Defenders of Plushville: In this light-gun-game, you find yourself in a mall and need to defend the wholesome build-a-teddy workshop from the Gorgonzola that escaped the supermarket down the hall!!
 Laser Bike: Ride down the beach at sundown, enter the city, and end up in space in this transformative racing game!
 Sheepy Runs: You want to eat some delicious looking flowers, but the local wolves want to eat some delicious looking you! Evade them in a labyrinth of hedges, and reach the highest score!


Quality of Life:

 The Arcade Mode is overhauled - select freely and go in-and-out of them at an instance!
 The Story is significantly extended - and actively accurately tracks your current relation to the Ghost!


Bugfixes

 Missing or misplaced colliders - no more!
 Missing or misplaced markers - no more!
 Inaccurate Jumping Witch jump height - no more!
 Misplaced Jumping Witch camera - no more!
 Ghost did not reach the position in 3D cutscene - no more!
 Ghost face flickered back and forth between normal and mad - no more!
 Player in Robot Time got stuck on ladders if using a controller as input - no more!
 The Hooked on Art and Laser Bike machines had flipped normals - no more!
 The heart and cloud particles whenever your relation changes in dialogue got abruptly deleted after a second  no more!
 And many more fixes! :D


For our future plans, after this week, we need a week or two to recover from Gamescom, and then we will get back to fixing stuff - because this is only a 1.0 after all!
Our efforts from now on will primarily focus on polishing, adding juice and fixing any bugs. The only significant new features we are still planning to add to the game are the following:

 Memory Items - going around the Arcade Hall, you can look for little hidden items that reveal part of a backstory - a story that will become complete if you find all 7 of them. The concept art, texturing and writing for this feature is done, but the 3D modeling, programming and sound design still need to be finished.
 Hooked on Art- we want to fundamentally redesign this Arcade Game, leading to a larger focus on gameplay as well as a satisfying culmination of all elements met throughout your journey - the game design has started for that, but the rest still needs to be done.


I think that is everything. Thanks for reading this, supporting us and maybe even buying this game - you are what keeps us going. We'll be on our way to Cologne now, so have fun, and we'll see you on the other side.

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - The Clean Update
notes.content:
Heyo, we are back from the dead! While it might have looked like we've taken a break, we've done the exact opposite of it - all our semester submissions piled up at once. However, not only are they over now, but since many of them were for this very game, we have a lot to share and show, and this is just a small part of that! 

But before we get into this...
We will be exhibiting at Gamescom in Cologne this year! That's right, we have a spot at the Indie Arena Booth from August 21st until August 25th thanks to the Hessen Foundation!
You can read about it in a (German) interview here: https://www.feelslikehessen.de/blog/haunted-arcade

And in addition to that... we will also be exhibiting at the GermanDevDays on August 7th and August 8th. Feel free to come visit our booth if you are around Frankfurt at that time! :D

Headlines:

 Watergun: At a certain part throughout the story, if you go to Shopkeep the Shopkeeper, who is usually located at the shop, you unlock the watergun. With it, you can shoot all the dirty Arcade Machines standing around the hall and clean them bit by bit! Feel free to try it out :) 
 Power: There is a mysterious new Powerbox in the Arcade Hall. Rumors have it that if the Ghost gets too huffy, he will just cut the power entirely and stop you from playing any more games. However, maybe Shopkeep can help you with that?
 Arcade Machines: While we're not quite ready to release the 4 new Arcade Games to the public yet, you can already spot the Machines in the hall - they are just locked for now! (Maybe some dedicated programmers could also figure out a way to unlock them and play an in-development alpha version?)


Quality of Life:

 Drama Llama Animation: When beating the boss of this game, there is a new animation of the Ghost getting defeated.
 A ton of Arcade machines have new, overhauled textures and designs!
 The credits now apprropriately show the new team members and their departments!


There are way too many bugfixes to count, and I am sure I am forgetting some quality of life changes as well, but that's alright! ... I tell myself.

Also, promise we have not forgotten about the bug list, and the passionate bug collectors that have formed for this game! We hear you and we will fix anything when we find the time between all the new features and organizational issues!

Okay, that's it for now, hope you have fun with the game!

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - The Quest Update
notes.content:
This update managed to break the weekly streak of content updates, but I hope that what it entails might help explain that decision :D For future changes and additions that seem simple on the surface, like enabling all games to be played in any order, or adding little objects that can be discovered and reveal the Ghost's backstory, the game needed a deeper restructure of central systems and addition of missing ones.
Which leads us straight to the headlines:

Headlines:

 Journal: Where you would usually find your Pause Menu, you will now find a journal! This journal features several pages that can be flipped between, one for Settings, one for Quests, and 2 more for upcoming content that you can already see hinted at. :)
 Quests: You will (hopefully) never feel lost again as there are Popups and Journal Entries for your current progression through the Main Quests. This will become especially useful as more and more objectives get added, and the progression becomes non-linear. Roads that desperately needed to be paved. :)
 Interactive Dialogue: The dialogue system has been restructured from the ground up, allowing for up to 3 Player Choices for responses at select moments. This allows the dialogue to branch into separate sub trees, and while you can already experience it right now, it will significantly flourish tied to the Relationship System in future Updates.   


Quality of life:

 You can us e the D-Pad to play the Arcade Games now.
 You can interact both with the East Face Button as well as the South Face Button now. On KBM, you can either use E or Enter.
 The framerate used to be capped to 60. That cap is gone now!
 There is a friendly disclaimer provided by the Ghost upon starting the game now, clarifying that due to this being an Early Access, contents are subject to change!

I know that some people have been asking for the ability of inverting the y-axis, and it is on my to-do list! I sadly did not get to it yet.

Bugfixes:

 Quitting out of the Jumping Witch game used to lead the camera back to Drama Llama instead of the player position - no more!
 Talking to the Ghost after the 1st and beore the 2nd game made the camera face the roof instead of the Ghost - no more!
 Some select players managed to either get stuck in dialogue or accidentally skip the last game entirely - no more! (hopefully lol)

I know there are always plenty more glitches and exploits to fix, and we will continue to do so! :D
Thank you to everyone who reports them and puts them on our list.




Finally, rest assured that we are currently holding back content as we are knees deep into all of the 4 upcoming Arcade Games. We want to deliver a complete experience of all 3 phases of the games in a polished state before releasing them to the public.

Oki thas it have fun and see ya arnd ^^ - Lem

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - The UI Update Part 1
notes.content:
This one's a bit outside of the Roadmap, but the main UI needed a lil' bit of a fresh coating, so here we go! :D
Why does it say Part 1? Well, in this one, the current UI is overhauled and adjusted, but in upcoming parts, new UI elements for quests will be added, a bond-meter for your relationship to the Ghost (which goes into the Interactive Dialogue Update), and more. For example, there's exciting new ideas for the Main Menu :D
But let's not get ahead of ourselves and stay at this one for now;

Headlines:

 All new UI Sprites for buttons, sliders, toggles, markers, button prompts, text boxes and more - both for the selected and unselected version! The entire primary UI has gotten a fresh new coating.
 There are two new Achievements available: One for buying your first Hat, and another one for equipping your first Texture Set via any of the spray cans you've unlocked! If you have a save where you have purchased spray cans already, you can easily get this Achievement by loading back into it and interacting with the unlocked can! 

Bugfixes:

 The movement of the Player mullet on the darker Air Hockey table was way slower and had a lot more drag - no more!


Bugs we are currently aware of and trying to fix in future versions:

 The sounds in the Arcade Hall overlap if you go back to the Menu
 The Ghost's path in the Hall sometimes interferes with objects in the environment
 You cannot open the Pause Menu while the button prompt for the Shop, Air Hockey or one of the Arcade Games shows up, instead, hitting the button will only open the Pause Menu once you've walked away from the button prompt


You can see our upcoming Roadmap right here:

Version 2.8: Interactive Dialogue

 Completely rewritten dialogue
 Pick-and-choose from different dialogue response options
 End up with different bonds depending on what you picked

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - The Air Hockey Update
notes.content:
Ever thought that you'd wish there was more to do in the Arcade Hall itself? That is a huge part of what we are working on, and as a first result of that work, the Air Hockey Minigame is finally here! 

Headlines:

 Air Hockey: Infinitely replay in matches against the Ghost AI! Can you beat him? Every goal you score will grant you a ticket for the Ticket Shop, and there is a new Achievement as well if you manage to win against the Ghost!
 Casual or 80s Mode: When you start a new game, it will now prompt you with the decision whether to play the game in Casual or 80s Mode: Do you want the authentic experience of having to play an Arcade Game all the way through or having to start it all over again, or would you say that game design has improved for a reason, and a few checkpoints within each Arcade Game are more than justified? You will have to make that decision before starting the game now - but do not worry, there is a toggle in the Pause Menu as well, so you can always re-decide!
 FOV Slider: We got you feedback that a portion of players felt irritated by the first person view of the 3D Hall, and someone on our Community Forum even pointed it out specifically - there is no way to adjust the Field of View of the player. Now, not only did we increase the default Field of View slightly, but we also added a slider into the Pause Menu which enables you to adjust it to your liking. 


Quality of life:

 Arrows have become Markers: Confused where to go or what to do next in the Hub Scene? Don't worry! There are UI Markers floating above anything that is currently interact-able in the Hub. If it is highlighted in green, you can use it right now! If it is red, however, you will have to progress further in the story to unlock it.
 Forward skipping through the game in the Hub Scene seems to have done more harm than good as players stumbled on it unintentionally and skipped parts of the game - so we took it out for now! Don't worry, you can still skip passages in Llama Drama and skipping in the Hub will return under a fresh new coat of skin!


Bugfixes:

 Continuing from a save did not update the Dialogue of the Ghost accordingly - now it does!
 There was a bright pink hat on the Ghost when continuing - no more!
 The Tickets UI overlapped with the Casual Mode toggle in the escape menu - no more!
 The Tickets UI stayed infinitely even if you are not in the shop and not getting any new tickets - no more (limited to 20s)!
 When pressing Continue, a new Hub Theme soundtrack started playing over the already started one - no more!
 Adjusting the Sensitivity also changed the volume - no more!

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - The Shop and Tickets Update
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44880589/bc8d96129343711661369d4e1c9bde05f6dd1e41.png

Surprise! We've decided to pull the first big part of the "Happy Hall Designer" Shop Update forwards and release it already so that you can have a bunch of new content! But do not fret - we did not forget to include other updates and bugfix as well!

Headlines:

 Themes: Customize your Arcade Hall by unlocking Themes with your hard earned Tickets. Unlock some Spray Cans in the Ticket Shop that transform the entire Hall into a moody setting of your choice. Be it the wavy-dreamy Aqua Set, the spooky scary Halloween Set, or the hot and poppy Girlyponk Set, feel free to try them out and see your Hall in a completely new light (literally)!
 Hats! Haats!! And more Haaats!!! Speaking of ways to spend those Tickets, here are 10 new Hats available in the Ticket Shop, some of which include a cute Duckie, an arguably even cuter Froggo, and so much more! Just come by there and explore the vast new selection!
 Furniture? We're cooking up something special for you in terms of customization, and the final result needs a little more time in the oven, but for now, there are 2 available pieces of Furniture! A hanging shelf and a cabinet. What can you do with them? If you walk up to them and interact, you will carry them around and you're able to place them anywhere they don't collide with another object in the Hall! 


Quality of life:

 It's all permanently saved now. All the hats you buy, all the Spray Cans you unlock, what hat you equip, what theme you use - they are all permanently stored now, and still available the next time you enter the game if you press "Continue". :)
 Jumping Witch did not give the players any tickets - those days are over! When you play Llama Drama, you get one ticket for every 100 points you earn in your score (and this stacks up when playing again and again) - and in Jumping Witch, you even get one ticket for 10 points!
 There are indicating Markers now that point at the currently active Arcade Game - so that you never get lost and always know where to go!
 In a similar spirit, at the very start of the game, the path you should not head down yet is a lot darker and less accessible now so that you do not get lost.
 We've conducted a user-testing and found that the majority of players found it annoying that the Ticket Shop automatically activates when walking close-by - and so we yeeted that out of the game! Now, you have to specifically interact with the shop when you see the button prompt in-front of the main desk - else nobody is showing up to serve you.


Bugfixes:

 The purple screen of death that sometimes popped up when talking to the Ghost  - no more!
 The Ghost never moved again after you left the Ticket Shop - no more!
 The Ghost became invisible and glitched out if you quit the Llama Drama game after getting to the 2nd phase - no more!
 If you tabbed out of the game on the Main Menu screen and then tabbed back in, or you miss-clicked next to one of the buttons when using a Mouse, no button would be selected anymore and you would be stuck - no more!
 The UI Sprite for Tickets is now a much more unified sprite with the design language of the rest of the UI!
 The Hidden Arcade Button works now and brings you to the Steam Page of that game!

notes.title: Haunted Arcade - Controller Update
notes.content:
We're trying to adapt the current version of the game to any feedback we get at the moment, and we've heard you. This update is trying to cater specifically towards features that players were missing or felt were incorrect, particularly regarding Gamepad Controls, but there are several new features for players on KBM as well. :)

Quality of life:

 Sensitivity Sliders: The default sensitivity on Gamepad controls is understandably too high for some of you, and you were missing control over it - that's why you can now customize your Sensitivity both for KBM as well as Controller/Gamepad via Sliders in the Main Menu under Settings, or in the Pause Menu directly.
 Remapped Gamepad-Controls: No more need for questions on how to enter the pause menu - we've tried to adapt to universal control standards on Gamepads. The pause Menu is now on the Start Button. Since you enter an Arcade Game with the East Face Button, you now quit it with the South Face Button (Nintendo Layout A/B, Playstation Layout Circle/X, XBox Layout B/A).  
 Enhanced Controls Screen: Several button inputs were still missing on the current Controls screen both for KBM as well as Gamepad in the Main Menu and Pause Menu - but they have been added to it now! Additionally, the current buttons have been updated and the new buttons for Gamepad controls have also been added to Controls Screens within the Arcade Games.
 Skipping: If you are replaying the game, or you get tired of all the Hub-Interactions, or you cannot get over one of the Arcade Games (though you could turn on Casual Mode from the Pause Menu), you can skip this part of the game entirely. To do that, just hit the F-Key on KBM or the right D-Pad Button on Gamepad Controls (skipping forwards, get it?).
Doing this in the Hub Area immediately upon starting the game skips the opening and turns on all the lights of the Arcade Hall. Doing it again after this skips the Llama Drama game and instantly triggers the post-game dialogue. Doing it again after that skips the Jumping Witch game and instantly triggers that post-game dialogue. And finally, doing it again after this skips the Hooked on Art game and instantly triggers the game's ending sequence.
Doing it in the first Arcade Game skips one level each time, skipping three times triggers the first twist, skipping three times again triggers the boss fight.
Feel free to play around with it and control what part of the game you want to play!


Bugfixes:

 Player gets pushed off at start of Hooked on Art when using Gamepad controls
 Skipping in Hub causes unexpected behavior while camera is disabled
 Missing Collider on Pinball Machine
 Flipped normals on Arcade Machine



That's all the news we've got for you for now. Don't worry, we're already hard at work on upcoming features!

notes.title: Haunted Arcade Update EA1.01 + Week 1 Patch
notes.content:
Thank you very much to everyone checking out the game and jumping into it! We value every piece of feedback very highly and are excited to push out our first (if small) feature-update tied-in with the Week One patch.

Quality of life:

 Casual Mode: We acknowledge that the harsh Game Design of the 1980s, forcing you to play through an entire game in one go, is not exactly up to today's standards. This is why you can now toggle on Casual-Mode both from the Main Menu as well as the Pause Menu to enable Checkpoints throughout the first two games. :)
 Controls-Screen: We have heard all of your requests, and it is finally here: Both from the Main Menu as well as the Pause Menu, you can now look at the Controls for both the Keyboard-Mouse layout as well as the controller layout. A huge thank-you to the users @EnchanterKC and @Yumyum36 for posting control guides to the Steam Reviews and the Community Hub in the meantime. :)
 There are 6 new models for decorative Arcade Machines standing around in the Hub Area, some of which replace former duplicates, and some of which replace faulty models entirely. They are of a much higher quality standard and feature fully hand-painted textures. They are the first public contribution from the newest members of our Development Team. Give it up for Hakon, Lucy and Leo! :D


Bugfixes from 1.01:

 Sound overlay when quitting to Main Menu (all sound gets stopped now)
 Camera Bug in Jumping Witch (Camera does not suddenly go out of bounds when replaying after your first try anymore)

notes.title: Haunted Arcade x Hidden Arcade - a Hidden Object Game!
notes.content:
The Steam Page for our free Tie-In Game has just been made public and you can wishlist Hidden Arcade right now! 
You can find the Steam Page here!

[previewyoutube=I1WCi2ALSvg;full][/previewyoutube]

What is Hidden Arcade?

There's a new wave of games in which you have to find 100 x (it"s mostly cute little cats) in an environment and each cat grants you an achievement. I absolutely love these little serotonin machines, and I have played far more of them than would be considered healthy. And maybe you have too, because these titles happen to be quite popular.

So what's better than finding 100 cute little blobs in one environment? Finding 300 cute little blobs in three environments!

That's right! You can dive into each of the currently available Arcade Games in Haunted Arcade and look for little Ghosts in them!

But why would you do that?

As you continued to play the Arcade Games, you happened to have so many high-scores in one of the machines that the name of the Ghost completely disappeared from the title screen. His score is now deleted... forever! Incapable of processing this devastating information, the Ghost physically falls apart and splits into 300 little pieces that spread throughout the 3 Arcade Games. Only you can find all the Ghost pieces and revive him from his current fate!

Feel free to wishlist the game now! :) We are planning to release it within this month.

You can find the Steam Page here!

notes.title: Early Access Release! What now?
notes.content:
The Early Access has finally launched! Thank you to everyone who is checking it out or considering.

The version you see right now was developed by 4 developers, Pauline Lechler, Emil Altan, Marianna Keim and me, Lemon Pohl.

While Marianna Keim has decided to leave our Development Team, our total numbers have doubled as Hakon Wind, Ken Sudermann, Leonie Droege, Maurizio Cavallo and Lucy Gebken have joined our ranks to work on any future versions of the game (they are already working on it and have come up with some very quick results).

Together, we are currently working on further Arcade Games as well as a Decorating Feature for the 3D Hub.

In detail, our plans are:

Use the tickets you earn by playing these games to acquire Hats or Helmets for the Ghost
Experience the story of connecting to the Ghost and solving the final
